html:
"Slavonic tribes" is the map's label, for the year 800, for the many Slavic-speaking peoples who then filled eastern Europe, from the Elbe to the upper Volga and down into the Balkans.

The Slavs spread out from somewhere north of the Carpathians from the 500s onward, filling lands left empty in the migrations after Rome's fall. Some moved south, and the settling of the Balkans reached as far as Greece. Others went west to the Elbe and east into the forests of what became Russia.

Around 800 they lived as farmers in small villages and wooden strongholds, in tribes with their own chiefs and gods such as Perun. Many had lived under the Avars, whose power the Franks broke in the 790s. Within a century larger states took shape among them: Great Moravia, where Cyril and Methodius brought a Slavic church, and to the east Kievan Rus. The map for 900 shows the Slavic tribes of central Europe at that next stage.
sum: "Slavonic tribes" is the map's label, for the year 800, for the many Slavic-speaking peoples who then filled eastern Europe, from the Elbe to the upper Volga and down into the Balkans.
